newsitem.title: BOLIVIA: Bolivia finds bones that could be Che Guevara's.
newsitem.headline: Bolivia finds bones that could be Che Guevara's.

text.p: A team of Cubans, Argentines and Bolivians searching for the remains of Ernesto "Che" Guevara in Bolivia has found bones that "very probably" belong to the legendary revolutionary, Bolivian officials said on Wednesday.
"We are probably very close to the result we have been seeking," said Marcos Tufino, the official coordinating the dig near the town of Villagrande in the jungle highlands of southeastern Bolivia.

Searchers have found half a dozen skeletons and among them a bone with apparent traces of formaldehyde, making experts think it could belong to Guevara, who was captured by Bolivian troops in 1967 and executed in a village schoolhouse.

"We now have six skeletons and one bone coloured slightly red...probably a humerus, which according to one of the Cuban scientists could be one of Che's bones," Tufino told a news conference in La Paz.
The Bolivian official said he hoped to have more details within hours, but he warned that definitive identification of the bones could take up to two weeks.

The search for the bones of the Argentine-born hero of the Cuban revolution, who died trying to export Cuban communism to the South American mainland, resumed in May near an airstrip outside Vallegrande, 480 miles (770 km) southeast of La Paz.
